obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices; reasonable data security)
basis: A for-profit software business selling subscriptions to businesses in 11 states, outside the statutory carve-outs in 45(a)(2), with no size threshold. It holds about 88,000 end-client records and makes public security and data-use statements

Booking pages are general-audience pages; parents book for children with their own details and there are no child profile fields, so the service is not directed to children under 13 and no actual knowledge of collecting their data appears

citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.140(d); Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7000 et seq.
basis: Not a 'business': about $180,000 a year in revenue, all from subscriptions; no personal information is bought, sold or shared; about 88,000 end-client records

No covered data transactions: every provider's terms name a U.S. contracting entity and there are no offshore contractors; the data is mostly contact data, and the 88,000 records are below the 100,000-person bulk threshold for covered personal identifiers (28 CFR 202.205(f))

obligation: Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act (PADFA)
basis: Not a data broker: revenue comes only from subscriptions, and no personal information is sold or transferred
Not a telecommunications carrier or VoIP provider; the company buys message delivery from an SMS provider
No federal agency customers; subscribers are small appointment-based businesses
A sole proprietorship, not a public company

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification; third-party agent duty)
basis: For end-client data the company maintains data for subscribers as a third-party agent (501.171(1)(h), (6)); for subscriber staff accounts it owns the data. About 61,000 end-client records and most subscribers are in Florida
Subscribers are in 11 states and end clients live in several states, so a breach could reach residents of other states

obligation: Terms of Service and DPA commitments (contract)
citation: Terms of Service and DPA; two negotiated DPAs
basis: Use only to provide the service; incident notice within 72 hours of confirmation, or 48 hours for the two negotiated DPAs; 14 days' notice of new sub-processors; deletion within 30 days after closure; export on request

obligation: HIPAA Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules
basis: Subscribers are salons, barbershops, pet groomers and home-cleaning services, not health care providers or health plans, and no business associate agreement is on file
Not a financial institution: the company sells booking software subscriptions

citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
applies: No (no card data in the platform)
basis: Card details are entered only on the payment processor's hosted checkout page; the company never receives, stores or transmits card numbers
Smart Replies drafts booking messages and makes no automated decision with significant or consequential effects on a person

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
basis: Final rule not published; tracked for planning

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
applies: Yes (only if a payment is considered)
basis: Applies to any U.S. person considering a payment to an extortionist
